{{Short description|One-dimensional data visualization}}
{{distinguish|Carpet plot}}
[[File:Comparison of 1D bandwidth selectors.png|right|thumb|A rug plot of 100 data points appears in blue along the x-axis.  (The points are sampled from the normal distribution shown in gray. The other curves show various [[kernel density estimation|kernel density estimates]] of the data.)]]
A '''rug plot''' is a [[Plot (graphics)|plot]] of data for a single quantitative variable, displayed as marks along an axis. It is used to visualise the distribution of the data. As such it is analogous to a [[histogram]] with zero-width bins, or a one-dimensional [[scatter plot]].

Rug plots are often used in combination with two-dimensional scatter plots by placing a rug plot of the x values of the data along the x-axis, and similarly for the y values. This is the origin of the term "rug plot", as these rug plots with perpendicular markers look like tassels along the edges of the rectangular "rug" of the scatter plot.
